Thanks for the design!
I have another idea in mind, that I think might be more user friendly. Here how it would go:

The button "Import CSV" would open a dialog. There we'd be able to either open a file (with a button or drag and drop) or paste some string, like you designed in the 2 tabs Paste CSV/Import CSV (except this would be in the dialog)

The dialog could also be triggered automatically by:
* drag and dropping a file on top of the view (we'd detect a drag is happening, and the view would change to a drop zone).
* Pasting something that "looks like" a CSV (for example it contains at least 2 lines).
Both these options would also open the dialog, pre-filled.

After CSV data has been processed, the same dialog would show how the parsed data looks like, still inside the dialog. At this point this would look like the enroll view, but with just the few first rows.
There the user could configure after the import how the CSV file looks like and the data would be reparsed to show the change.
Things I'm thinking about (not all may be needed right now):
Reordering the columns
Delimiter tab or character, and selection of character (french may use ; instead of , so it's important for us)
Keep the first row or ignore it
If more than 3 columns, be able to pick specific columns (this could also allow to ignore columns more generally, and import just 2 values for each row even though they have 3 or more).
Specify OUs through their name or IDs

At this point I'm not so sure what to do. A CSV could have hundreds of rows, and I'm not sure we want to show them all in the view... So we might want to trigger the import right from the dialog... And that could mean that we could force-set a OU to all items for example. Or just to all the ones where the OU is incorrect? If the OU is incorrect for those users, instead of erroring we could add them without an OU at all, or show an error explaining the issue (maybe this could be configured too so that the admin is in control).

What I like with this dialog + configuration is that the user will see what the configuration does. Also I believe this would work better when the CSV contains a ton of rows.

So here are my (a little more than) 2 cents. Tell me what you think!

I'll start implementing something like this now so would love your feedback :)
